title: WordScript Model Catalogue
description: Schema for the one versioned model catalogue both runtimes read (ADR 0115, scoped by ADR 0120). A row records what a vendor documents about a model, with the source and read-date docs/PROVIDERS.md requires. It never records what this build can operate: that is core::providers::model_capabilities, and a catalogued model with no adapter answers unknown.

version.description: Catalogue schema version. Bump on incompatible changes; core::model_catalogue asserts against it. 2 adds the optional `install` block (ADR 0122) — additive, and there is no migration because there is no on-disk state: the file is compiled into the binary through include_str!. 3 adds `reasoning_effort` (ADR 0214), and it is a bump rather than a quiet addition because a reader that ignores the field sends no effort to a reasoning model and gets an empty completion back: the field is absorbed or the row does not work.

providers.description: Every vendor id a row may name. A provider here need not be registered in core::providers::registry — a row is catalogued before its adapter exists, which is the state ModelSupport::Unknown was created for.

id.description: The vendor id. Where an adapter exists this is the registry's canonical id.

lane.description: Which lane this vendor is drawn in.

models.description: The catalogue proper. One row per model this build routes to, defaults to, or makes a statement about (ADR 0120) — not every id a vendor serves.

id.description: The stable slug every consumer names this row by. Deliberately not the model id: a vendor's next generation changes model_id and leaves every reference standing.

role.description: Which of the three roles this model serves. Same vocabulary as core::providers::ProviderRole (ADR 0105), so the schema does not invent a second one.

model_id.description: What goes on the wire — or, where no request shape exists yet, the drawn label, with a note saying so.

streaming.description: What the VENDOR DOCUMENTS about streaming for this model's role: transcription for a speech row, synthesis for a voice row. Same vocabulary as core::providers::ModelSupport (ADR 0110). It is not what this build can operate and must never be read as that — the local rows are the live example, documented as streaming while the adapter answers Unsupported.

languages.description: What the source says about language coverage, in its own terms. Prose rather than codes, because the sources answer in prose and a code list would invent precision.

source.description: Where the row was read. A vendor URL, or a path in this repo where the claim's provenance is this repo's own drawing or runtime — which is stated rather than dressed up as a vendor reading.

read_date.description: The date the source was read, ISO 8601.

reasoning_effort.description: How much the model may think before it answers, where it is a reasoning model and the vendor takes the parameter. ABSENT MEANS THE PARAMETER IS NOT SENT, which is the right answer for every model that does not reason — sending it to one that does not is a request a vendor may refuse. It is here rather than in the adapter because it is a fact about a model (ADR 0115), and it is load-bearing rather than a tuning knob: an unconstrained reasoning model spends the completion budget thinking and returns an empty string, which on this product is a dictation that silently loses its cleanup.

note.description: What the columns cannot carry about this row. Sparse on purpose: the prose survey is docs/PROVIDERS.md and this file does not become a second one.

install.description: How this model gets onto this machine, where that is a question about this row at all (ADR 0122). Absent is the answer for every hosted lane rather than an omission: there is nothing to install for Groq or OpenAI, and a surface asking them is asking the wrong lane. Two variants because there are two mechanisms and they do not share a disk — WordScript downloads the speech weights into a directory it manages, and asks the server the user runs to pull the language ones. Carries its own source and read-date: a weights repository that moves a file breaks an install rather than a claim, so these facts are dated like every other row here.

url.description: Where the weights are fetched from. Followed through redirects; the file this lands is WordScript's own.

file_name.description: What the file is called in the managed directory. Stated rather than derived from the URL, because core::providers::local resolves a recogniser by the ggml-{stem}.bin shape and a URL is free to be spelled any way at all.

size_bytes.description: The exact size, so free space can be checked before the first byte is requested and the drawn size is a fact rather than an estimate.

sha256.description: Checked against the .part file before it is renamed into place. The reason the row carries a checksum and not only a size: there must be no window in which half a model is spelled like a whole one.

runtime.description: Which server is asked. WordScript owns none of these files and never places one beside them.

tag.description: What the server is asked to pull. Carried beside model_id and never derived from it: qwen2.5:7b-instruct and qwen2.5-7b-instruct are not the same string, and rewriting the punctuation would be a guess dressed as a lookup.

size_bytes.description: What the pull costs on the server's disk, summed over the manifest's layers.

quantization.description: The drawn library's second literal, beside the size. Stated by the tag itself wherever a quantized tag exists, so this column and the tag cannot drift apart.

runtime_defaults.description: Which row each of the runtime's model defaults resolves to. This is the half of the file the Rust config reads; nothing here is a drawing.

lanes.description: What the AI Models matrix offers per lane and job, by row id. The half of the file the drawing reads. A lane or job absent here is a lane or job that offers no picker — Self-hosted types its model id, and the listening jobs on Enterprise say which lane can run them instead.

default.description: The row drawn as chosen. Must appear in `offered`.

offered.description: The rows the picker lists, in drawn order.
